title: Automated shadow-telemetry fail-fast and runbook consolidation for canary rollouts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
A canary rollout on 2026-02-25 exposed a subtle regression in tail-latency and generation quality for the q4-quantized variant when under steady-state shadow traffic. The incident was contained by manual rollback but highlighted gaps in our shadow telemetry (sampling, signal alignment), runbook coverage, and the absence of a reliable fail-fast automation that can safely roll back a bad model variant during an active canary.

Objective:
1) Consolidate the multiple ad-hoc postmortem runbooks into a single, prescriptive 'canary fail-fast' runbook that on-call engineers can follow within 15 minutes of detection.
2) Implement an automated shadow-telemetry pipeline + rules engine to surface masked regressions earlier and trigger a safe auto-rollback when thresholds are breached.
3) Add preflight synthetic smoke tests to the canary controller to reduce noisy false positives from workload variance.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: telemetry collection (shadow + canary), rules engine, runbook consolidation, dashboarding, alerting, automatic rollback controller with hysteresis, and integration tests against the rollout orchestration.
- Out of scope: model training changes, quantization tooling, and long-term ML eval suite expansion (these will be tracked in separate PM tickets).

Acceptance criteria:
- New consolidated runbook available in Confluence and linked from the Console's rollout page.
- Shadow telemetry pipeline captures request/response hashes, p95/p99 latency, token error rate, and a lightweight quality signal (synthetic eval score) for both shadowed and baseline variants for every canary window.
- Rules engine implements three signal checks (latency tail, errors, synthetic-quality delta) with configurable thresholds and a configurable evaluation window (default 5 minutes).
- Auto-rollback controller triggers an automated rollback when any two of the three signals exceed thresholds for two consecutive evaluation windows, with a 30s cool-down and operator-notify step.
- Integration tests covering deliberate regressions are added to CI; manual tabletop run scheduled with SRE/PM/Oncall.

Failure thresholds (initial defaults, tuned after rollout):
- p95 latency increase vs baseline > 30% absolute AND p99 > 1000ms
- error rate increase (5xx or protocol errors) > 0.5 percentage points absolute
- synthetic-eval score drop > 3.0 points relative to baseline sample

Trade-offs and rationale:
- We prefer a conservative multi-signal rule (2-of-3) to avoid noisy auto-rollbacks triggered by transient spikes in latency or sampling variance. This trades a slightly slower rollout reaction for fewer false rollbacks.
- Synthetic-eval is intentionally lightweight (fast inference on a small evaluation set) to keep detection windows short. It will not replace the full offline eval pipeline but acts as an early-warning guardrail.
- Auto-rollback includes operator notification and an option to require manual approval for P1 customers; this balances automation with customer impact control.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for rules engine thresholding and hysteresis logic.
- End-to-end test that deploys a canary in the staging environment, injects synthetic latency and quality regressions, and asserts the controller performs the rollback and posts audit events.
- Load test to validate telemetry ingestion at the expected shadow traffic scale (up to 10% of production traffic for a single canary).
notes: 2026-02-25 - Incident: Canary q4-quant variant rollout caused 2.3x p99 increase for a subset of shard traffic; manual rollback executed by on-call (Ethan Zhou) at 11:42 UTC. Initial triage pointed to degraded KV-cache warmup behavior under continuous shadowing.

runbook_snippet:
Immediate detection flow:
1) Alert fires from rules engine (2-of-3 signal breach confirmed for 2 consecutive windows).
2) Controller posts message to #rollouts-alerts with summary (signals, timestamps, sample ids) and creates an audit event in Trace.
3) Controller executes 'soft rollback' (reduce new-canary weight to 0 over 30s) and pauses further rollouts.
4) On-call runs quick verification checklist: verify rollback completed, compare baseline vs shadow sample traces, check KV-cache hit rates, check memory growth.
5) If rollback successful, assign follow-ups to model-owner and SRE, open postmortem with prioritized action items and ETA for fixes.
6) If auto-rollback fails (controller error), escalate to SRE pager and execute manual rollback runbook.
Operational notes: the controller logs all decisions; a kibana query for audit events exists and is linked from the runbook.
